content.text: I’ve read the orchestration MCP path end to end now: tool registration, HTTP host, main-to-renderer bridge, renderer workspace ownership checks, spawn behavior, and the regression tests. I’m doing one quick targeted test run so the summary can distinguish intended behavior from currently verified behavior.

I read the full orchestration MCP implementation.

The orchestration MCP is a built-in, per-session MCP server that exposes these tools when the `orchestration` domain is enabled:

- `orchestration_create_agent`
- `orchestration_send_prompt`
- `orchestration_list_agents`
- `orchestration_read_agent`
- `orchestration_read_run_outputs`
- `orchestration_wait_agents`
- `orchestration_close_agent`
- `orchestration_close_run`

Core files read:

- [createBuiltInMcpServer.ts](/Users/juliusolsson/Desktop/Development/agent-code/src/mcp/runtime/createBuiltInMcpServer.ts)
- [BuiltInMcpHttpHost.ts](/Users/juliusolsson/Desktop/Development/agent-code/src/mcp/runtime/BuiltInMcpHttpHost.ts)
- [OrchestrationBridge.ts](/Users/juliusolsson/Desktop/Development/agent-code/src/main/orchestration/OrchestrationBridge.ts)
- [orchestrationMcp.ts](/Users/juliusolsson/Desktop/Development/agent-code/src/renderer/src/workspace/orchestrationMcp.ts)
- [orchestrationTypes.ts](/Users/juliusolsson/Desktop/Development/agent-code/src/mcp/shared/orchestrationTypes.ts)
- [orchestrationPrompt.ts](/Users/juliusolsson/Desktop/Development/agent-code/src/mcp/shared/orchestrationPrompt.ts)
- [pane.ts](/Users/juliusolsson/Desktop/Development/agent-code/src/renderer/src/workspace/hook/actions/pane.ts)
- [test-orchestration-mcp.ts](/Users/juliusolsson/Desktop/Development/agent-code/scripts/test-orchestration-mcp.ts)

High-level shape:

The MCP server runs inside Agent Code main over loopback HTTP, with a bearer token scoped to each agent session. When a parent agent calls an orchestration tool, main does not mutate workspace state directly. It sends an `orchestration:request` IPC event to the renderer, because the renderer owns real workspace placement, Dispatch state, metadata, tab affinity, and persistence.

The renderer creates real Claude/Codex child sessions, usually detached into Dispatch under the parent’s project tab. Children get metadata like `orchestrationParentId`, `orchestrationRootId`, `orchestrationRunId`, and `orchestrationRole`. Reads and closes are ownership-gated so a parent can only coordinate its own children or descendants in the same orchestration root.

Important behavior:

- Child agents inherit parent context by default through provider transcript duplication or cross-provider transcript translation.
- The child receives a visible `<orchestration-handoff>` bootstrap prompt so it knows it is a new child agent, not the parent continuing.
- If inheritance fails, creation degrades to a clean child and the bootstrap prompt says duplicated context was unavailable.
- Reads intentionally cut inherited transcript history at the latest handoff marker, so parent output does not leak as the child’s result.
- `wait_agents` polls until matching children leave active states, then returns statuses and outputs.
- MCP-closed children get short-lived tombstones in main so a parent can still observe “closed” instead of the child disappearing immediately.
- Prompt delivery has provider-specific handling: Codex waits for readiness before paste+submit; Claude waits for paste placeholder before Enter.

I also ran the targeted regression test:

```bash
npm run test:orchestration-mcp -- --runInBand
```

It passed.

content.text: There are unrelated local changes already in the tree, so I’ll leave them alone and only touch the orchestration MCP files. The GitHub CLI is authenticated enough to resolve the repo, so after the code change I’ll try to create the follow-up issue directly.

The removal needs to happen at two layers: the MCP contract should stop advertising inheritance as usable, and the renderer spawn path should stop cloning/translating transcripts even if an old caller passes `inheritParentContext`. I’m making that explicit in code comments so the follow-up issue has a clear re-entry point.

gh issue create --title "Rebuild orchestration context inheritance on a stable provider contract" --body-file - <<'EOF'
## Problem

The original orchestration context inheritance path is being removed from the active MCP behavior because it is too unstable for real child-agent work.

The old implementation attempted to duplicate or translate the parent provider transcript, resume the child from that cloned transcript, then rely on a bootstrap handoff marker and transcript cut points to separate inherited context from the child's actual output. In practice this was fragile:

- child agents could retain stale parent identity or continue from the wrong conversational frame
- provider resume behavior differed between Claude and Codex
- stale parent answers could be surfaced as child outputs
- reads needed brittle handoff-marker cut points to recover the child work product
- delivery/readiness races made prompt-delivery accounting hard to trust

## Current state

The removal PR disables inheritance for orchestration-created agents. Children now start from clean provider conversations, and parents must include required context explicitly in the prompt.

The old `inheritParentContext` schema field may remain tolerated for compatibility with stale MCP tool caches, but it should be ignored until this issue is resolved.

## Goal

Bring back orchestration context inheritance only after there is a stable contract that proves a child can receive parent context without inheriting parent identity or corrupting output reads.

## Acceptance criteria

- Define a provider-neutral context handoff model that does not depend on resuming a child as if it were the parent.
- Preserve separate child transcripts and never append child work to the parent transcript.
- Make child output reads unambiguous without relying on fragile inherited transcript cut points.
- Cover same-provider and cross-provider launches for Claude and Codex.
- Include regression tests for nested orchestration, stale parent answers, failed inheritance, follow-up prompts, and closed/read output behavior.
- Only re-enable `inheritParentContext` after the behavior is stable enough to expose through MCP again.
EOF
